thought.text: All containers are healthy, volumes exist, and the Next.js build is complete. Let me verify the build args were baked into the client bundle and check a few more endpoints.

reasoning_content:
The Next.js build is in place, the media and uploads volumes have been created, and the containers are all healthy and up. Grepping for environment variables baked into the bundle didn't turn up anything — maybe the chunk structure is different. Let me check where the NEXT_PUBLIC variables were baked in (Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* into the static chunks). Let me search more broadly.

Also, the git log shows a commit called "d170d74 CHANGE – ..." — interestingly, it suggests there's a modified commit. Let me check whether the repository has been modified compared to upstream. Actually, git status shows that the only untracked file is docker-compose.noresources.yml (the workaround file, as expected). The top commit being "CHANGE – users.read..." might just be the state of the repository itself. Not important.

Let me verify that the build arguments are baked into the bundle, and check whether the middleware is working (the fact that the domain routing worked already suggests it is). Also, I'll do a simple check on whether the API is working, e.g., the payload collections endpoint. I'll also verify that the mailpit UI is up.

One more thing to check: the guide says `docker compose ps # wait for healthy` — web is healthy, mongo is also healthy, and mailpit is healthy too. Hocuspocus doesn't have a healthcheck defined in the compose (there's no healthcheck for the hocuspocus service — correct, it just needs to be Up).

Let me check whether the bundle contains the built-in URL.
